p1.text: You are an apprentice word wizard, and wizards do not grow old. A word said with meaning is a spell.

p2.text: Tonight you are summoned to an old courtyard in Moscow, Russia. The lamps are dark.

p3.text: A curse called the Silence has stolen this courtyard's words. Where the words went, everything froze.

p4.text: Learn Russian words from the people here. Cast them as spells to wake the courtyard, and open the gate to the city.

p5.text: Meet Eeskra, a spark of living language. She will be your guide.

h1.text: This is Moscow, today, and it has gone quiet. A curse called the Silence is stealing its words, from its very first day.

h2.text: Where it reaches, people stop understanding each other. A feast cannot begin. A book cannot be printed. A street on fire cannot call for help.

h3.text: You are an apprentice word wizard, and wizards do not grow old. A word said with meaning is a spell.

h4.text: First, you train. Iskra, a spark of living light, will teach you in her Study, and every word you learn makes you stronger.

h5.text: Then you step through her paintings into Moscow’s past, and give each moment its words back. It begins in 1147, at a feast.

h11.text: Moscow, 1147. Prince Yuri of Suzdal is at war for Kyiv, and he has invited his ally Svyatoslav to a place called Moscow. A chronicler writes the invitation down: the first time we know of that the city is named.

h12.text: Moscow, 1564. Church books copied by hand were full of mistakes, so Tsar Ivan ordered a house built for printing them. Here at the Print Yard, after almost a year of work, Ivan Fyodorov and Pyotr Mstislavets are finishing Moscow’s first dated printed book.

h13.text: Moscow, September 1812. Napoleon has invaded Russia, and after the battle of Borodino the Russian army has left Moscow without a fight. Most of its people have gone. Now the French march in, and fires break out across the city.

today.text: Moscow, today. You have carried its words through nine centuries. One old courtyard is still silent.

study.text: Welcome, apprentice. This is Iskra's study, a room outside time, where your training begins. Each painting on its wall is a door to a year of Moscow.

next11.text: In 1156 Yuri gave the hill wooden walls. That fort grew into the Kremlin. In 1547 Ivan was crowned the first tsar. The Kremlin's walls of 1495 stand today.

next12.text: Both printers were driven out of Moscow. Fyodorov printed a primer in Lviv, 1574. In 1581 he printed the Bible in Ostroh. The Print Yard now houses a university.

next13.text: Napoleon waited in vain for peace. He left on 19 October and lost his army. By 1817 Moscow had a new city plan. Its rubble made a grotto by the Kremlin.
